rv.q: Particularly when Parsons or Hecht is onstage, Harvey is a sweet treat.

Mr. Parsons brings a gentle, disarming sweetness to Elwood, and his performance grows in assurance and depth as the evening progresses. He makes Elwood's philosophical musings about life and friendship sound both heartfelt and freshly minted.
Not to worry, though, for no sooner does he rev the engine than "Storefront Church" starts roaring down the track.
The nuttier the farce becomes, in fact, the better this show is.
So is any real reason to see it.
He is so convincing in his give-and-take with Harvey that we almost begin to see the mischievous sprite.
It's good and often silly fun, greatly enriched by Parson's performance.
As a gentle ode to acceptance and nonconformity, “Harvey” is enjoyable — no more, no less.
Harvey remains a well-crafted, cute play with a terrific leading role.
Alas, the same might be said of Scott Ellis' oddly sluggish production, which lurches from scene to scene when it should be bunny-hopping briskly along.

It's thin stuff and difficult to pull off because a lot of the action happens offstage and is merely recounted, but this production has moments, while not really soaring into the absurdist yet warming stratosphere.

cn.t: Jim Parsons charms in this uneven revival of Mary Chase's Pulitzer-winning comedy, with critics praising his sweet, sincere performance while finding Scott Ellis' production somewhat dull and lacking compelling reason to revisit the 1944 chestnut.

sg.ra: SeatPlan names Center Orchestra rows E-G as the best seats overall, citing 'a winning mix of perfect proximity and elevated view over the heads in front' on a good rake with a low stage. Headout notes the 'outstanding inclination' keeps sightlines clear from middle rows. AVFMS Row D seat 2: 'Perfect view with unlimited legroom.' 16-row section seats ~350 of the 413 total; low stage means front rows don't require neck strain.

SeatPlan explicitly names Left and Right Mezzanine as 'the best value seats at the Laura Pels Theatre,' citing cheap tickets vs. central Orchestra with 'a clear and close view.' Only 3 rows (AA/BB/CC), under 100 seats — feels intimate and close to stage. Headout confirms 'very little restriction from the Mezzanine overhang at the back' of the Orchestra, meaning the Mezzanine itself is close/low. Row BB flagged by Headout as a specific value row.
